critical_operation.description: complete_io loops until the handshake completes or an error occurs. When the peer sends a ClientHello followed immediately by a close_notify alert, process_new_packets() consumes the alert, leaving is_handshaking() true while wants_read() and wants_write() are both false and eof is still false. None of the return arms at the bottom of the loop match: `(_, true, false)` needs the handshake to be finished, `(true, true, true)` needs eof, so `(..) => {}` falls through and the loop repeats forever, pinning a thread at 100% CPU. The 0.23.5 fix adds `if !self.wants_write() && !self.wants_read() { return Ok((rdlen, wrlen)); }` at the top of the loop, so a state that cannot progress returns instead of spinning. The upstream regression test feeds exactly this ClientHello+close_notify byte sequence and expects io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof.

entry_point.description: complete_io is the public blocking-IO driver used by rustls::Stream and rustls::StreamOwned. It is called after a blocking read or write and is responsible for driving the handshake; it is the first-and-only entry point for the affected path, and the advisory states that tokio-rustls and rustls-ffi do not call it and are not affected.
